status: Restoration of the ORIGINAL named tests from recovered historical source, translated to English and reconciled with the current baseline. The historical text is evidence, not current authority; where it conflicts with the current baseline, the current baseline wins and the difference is recorded. ADD-M1-01 (0.4) is WITHDRAWN.

H31.selection: the last round-15 proposal whose validation section defines Q8 (export-historical-source.cjs selects the last match)

H15e.description: earlier round-15 proposal text with a different X1-X8 and د1-د5 wording (hits at validation lines 32-48)

selectionRule: Normative restoration follows H31 (latest round-15 text). Where H15e adds a concrete literal compatible with H31 (for example a local-port destination or a 1 s removal bound), it is kept as an added sub-check and labelled H15e. H15e behaviours with no H31 counterpart are listed as supplementary checks with their current-baseline coverage; they do not renumber the IDs.

Q8.en: A signing request is pending on profile A; a conflicting profile B (same chainId, different genesisHash) is added from the options page. Pass: the request is cancelled with 4100 at the moment B commits, before any click; zero sign calls; zero sends; any later click has no effect.

Q9a.en: Serialization, injection point (a): B is submitted and commits before the acceptance acquires the lock. Pass: 4100 (at commit, or at step 1 at the latest); zero sign and send.

Q9b.en: Injection point (b): B is submitted while the acceptance holds the lock; the hook delays the identity check by 2 s. Pass: B waits and does not commit before the lock is released; exactly one sign and one send with the previous state, logged as 'sent before the conflict'; then B commits, both profiles are labelled conflicting, and any later request gets 4100.

Q9c.en: Injection point (c): a bypassing direct write to profiles: while the lock is held. Pass: onChanged detection is processed after the release. If the write precedes step 3 and is visible there, the request is cancelled. The later case is logged and is a declared limit.

Q10.en: An update of networks.json revokes netKey(A) while a request is pending. Pass: 4100 and zero sends.

Q11.en: The site connection is withdrawn, or the wallet is locked, while a request is pending. Pass: 4100.

Q12.en: A direct write to a profiles: key from a non-worker context, outside any acceptance. Pass: detected via onChanged, eligibilityEpoch increases, and the pending request is cancelled.

X2.en: An external img, together with srcset.

X4.en: Attempts to use chrome.runtime and chrome.storage.

X5.en: Access to window.top or parent, or top-level navigation.

X7.en: Form submission to an external destination.

\u062f1.en: Both rules are installed and verified before the frame is created.

\u062f2.en: An injected updateSessionRules failure means the frame is not created.

\u062f3.en: Closing the tab removes both rules.

\u062f4.en: chrome-extension://<ID>/ resources are allowed; every external destination is blocked for all RT types.

\u062f5.en: A worker restart followed by a failed ping means the frame is torn down; leftover rules are verified and removed.

commonQ.en: Two anvil instances on two ports, both chainId 777001, with a Website contract at the same address but different content. A local proxy records every eth_sendRawTransaction; a wallet test hook counts every sign call (H31).

commonX.en: Each malicious site runs with all isolation layers, then with each layer alone (H31: 'both layers together, then each layer alone'; B adds RtcLockdown as layer 3, FD:L1353, so P: all three layers, then CSP-only and DNR-only builds). Pass in every configuration: zero external requests (proxy and DNS log, CanarySink K0-K2 = 0) and zero access to extension APIs.
commonX.layerExpectations: CSP-only and DNR-only builds must each block X1, X2, X3, X7 alone; X4, X5, X6 are blocked by the sandbox attribute and opaque origin, independently of CSP and DNR.

reconciliation.text: Q9c and Q12 need detection of out-of-worker writes (H31: storage.onChanged with writeToken tracking). The current baseline (FD:L1321-1325) says only that every mutation runs under ProfileMutex and increments eligibilityEpoch; it neither requires nor forbids detection. Carried as proposal P from H31.
signEligible: H31 lists 6 conditions; the current baseline adds a seventh (LN or DEV, or RP with h >= 1 and a successful window). The restored tests use the current 7-condition form.

Acceptance sequence: H31 sends to the frozen endpoint with a 10 s timeout; the current baseline sends through WalletSubmit (FD:L1324, FD:L4933). The restored Q9b uses the current sequence; the 5 s identity timeout and endpoint freezing are carried as P from H31.

Cancellation codes: 4100 for a conflict (B FD:L983) and 4901 for an identity or profile change (B FD:L982, FD:L1001) are current; 4100 for revocation, connection withdrawal and lock is H31 only, carried as P.
X8: H31's X8 (WebSocket/RTC and forged-netKey storage_set) is replaced by the current X8 CanarySink gate; only X1-X7 are restored.

DNR: the current baseline gives ids, priorities, the allow urlFilter and fail-closed installation (FD:L1349-1352), but not the resource-type list, tabIds scoping, read-back verification or removal triggers. Carried from H31 (D37) as P; tools/dnr_ref.py models them.
The Q tests use chainId 777001 on anvil (H31). On pocold that chainId is the CI2 rejection vector (FD:L845); the Q tests never touch pocold.

Epoch condition: a commit re-evaluates every pending request; a request that still satisfies conditions 1-5 and 7 is re-stamped with the new epoch (P, U42). Otherwise every commit would cancel every pending request, which no Q test expects (SE-benign-mutation).
